hints.title: Subproblem Cardinality Obstacle
hints.text: Choosing k numbers out of 1 through n requires avoiding combinations with identical elements in different orders. How can advancing indices strictly forward enforce canonical combinations?

hints.title: Ascending Index Invariant
hints.text: Always select candidate numbers strictly greater than the last selected number to guarantee that each k-combination is generated in sorted order exactly once.

hints.title: Pruned Bounded Recursion Procedure
hints.text: Track current starting number start and current combination path. If len(path) == k, save a copy. Loop i from start up to n - (k - len(path)) + 1. Append i, recurse with i + 1, and pop.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Number of combinations is (n choose k), with O(k) time to copy each completed path.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all permutations of length k and sorting duplicates causes combinatorial blowup.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Path buffer of size k requires O(k) auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Pruning the loop boundary using remaining needed count n - need + 2.
